hyps.why: Replacing a removed input edge with a 3x3 conv restores connectivity and gives a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Adding a conv where the edge was cut gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
Edge 5 feeds the output node directly, so restoring it with a conv helps more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing none with a conv adds capacity and a path to the output, which beats a swap between existing ops.
Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a conv gains more than replacing skip or pooling.
Restoring a cut first edge with any conv gives a large gain, more than a swap.
Connecting node 2 to the output with a conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
A skip on an empty edge adds a gradient-friendly shortcut, whereas replacing a conv with skip loses capacity.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 is reached only via node 1, so the conv on edge 0 carries more of the signal.
With edge 4 absent there is less redundancy into the output, so a strong conv on edge 5 matters more.
